editorial.verdict: A computerized Singer Heavy Duty with LCD stitch selection and a metal-frame claim; owner reports on build and reliability are mixed.
editorial.whoFor: A beginner who wants push-button stitch selection, an LCD readout and six one-step buttonhole styles at the low end of the computerized Heavy Duty line.
editorial.skipIf: You want an automatic thread cutter, a walking foot in the box, or a published stitch count; Singer gives 215 applications and no count.
editorial.keySpec: 1000 spm (manual) · 215 stitch applications (claim) · 15.4 lb · 6 mm foot lift
strengths: Singer's manual publishes 0 to 7.0 mm stitch width, 0 to 4.5 mm length and a 6 mm presser foot lift.
Owners report the machine as quiet and smooth, one comparing it favourably with an older family machine.
Weight (15.4 lb) and dimensions (17.3 x 7.5 x 11.0 in) come from Singer's own manual.
weaknesses: Owners report build quality doubts, including one saying the machine is not fully metal despite the published metal interior frame.
Owners report defects such as an EL error on day one, a needle sticking in the down position and pedal faults (PatternReview, Walmart threads).
No automatic thread cutter and no walking foot in the box; Singer publishes no stitch count and a speed that differs between its own pages.

faqs.q: How many stitches does the Singer 6600C have?
faqs.a: Singer advertises 215 stitch applications and publishes no separate stitch count, so the built-in figure is [verify]. Dealers quote 100 and one comparison site 200. Applications count techniques, not patterns.

faqs.q: What is the throat space on the 6600C?
faqs.a: Singer's bundle page says 6.4 in throat space and does not say whether that is needle to body, so we hold it as [verify]. It is not in the manual's spec table.

faqs.q: How fast does the Singer 6600C sew?
faqs.a: Singer's manual gives 1000 +/- 50 stitches per minute at default length. A Singer Canada page excerpt says up to 1,100, so the two maker documents disagree.

faqs.q: Does the 6600C have an automatic thread cutter?
faqs.a: None is published. The manual lists a manual thread knife, and one comparison site lists the automatic cutter as a 6800C feature.

faqs.q: How much does the Singer 6600C weigh?
faqs.a: 15.4 lb, converted from the 7 kg in Singer's manual. Size is 17.3 x 7.5 x 11.0 in, converted from 440 x 190 x 280 mm.

faqs.q: What presser feet come with the 6600C?
faqs.a: Singer lists all-purpose, zipper, buttonhole, blind hem and satin stitch feet, plus 4 Class 15 bobbins. No walking foot is listed.

It is sold into that market: LCD stitch selection, a top drop-in bobbin and a built-in needle threader. Owners report defects such as pedal, bobbin winding and error faults, so check the return terms.

faqs.q: Can the 6600C sew denim and canvas?
faqs.a: Singer's copy says it is designed with heavy duty projects in mind, from denim to canvas, which is a claim. One owner reports loud noise and needle shaking at thick folded denim seams.
Singer's warranty page lists the 6600C Heavy Duty under Limited 25/1 Year. Some retailer copy quotes 2 years on electrical parts, so confirm the term with the seller.
Singer's standalone 6600C page redirects to its homepage, but the extension-table bundle page (6600CTABLE) is live. That is a page status, not a stated end of production.
